subject: pathology
title: Oesophagus and stomach: reflux, Barrett and gastric cancer

steps.tx: **Achalasia** is a motility disorder where myenteric neurons are lost, so the lower oesophageal sphincter fails to relax properly. Peristalsis also fails in the oesophageal body, so food and fluid collect above the tight sphincter for years. Barium imaging shows a dilated oesophagus tapering smoothly into a **bird beak narrowing** at the lower sphincter level. Chagas disease can destroy myenteric neurons similarly, and long standing achalasia raises squamous cancer risk over decades.
steps.say: Achalasia is a motility disorder where the lower sphincter fails to relax because myenteric neurons are lost gradually. Food retention occurs because aperistalsis prevents the oesophageal body from pushing contents into the stomach effectively. Barium imaging helps clinicians recognise the smooth distal tapering called bird beak narrowing.

steps.tx: This barium swallow shows a widely dilated contrast filled oesophagus that tapers smoothly at the lower sphincter. That smooth distal narrowing is the **bird beak sign**, and it reflects failed sphincter relaxation in **achalasia** rather than malignant obstruction. Retained contrast above the taper explains dysphagia for both solids and liquids from early in this motility disorder. Examiners contrast this smooth taper with an irregular shouldered stricture that would suggest oesophageal cancer instead.
steps.say: This barium study shows a dilated oesophagus because contrast collects above a sphincter that fails to relax properly. Bird beak tapering is smooth because achalasia narrows the sphincter without forming an irregular malignant mass. This appearance helps clinicians separate motility failure from cancerous obstruction in dysphagia stems.

steps.tx: Chronic **gastro oesophageal reflux** inflames the distal oesophagus and produces heartburn, strictures and columnar metaplasia over time. In **Barrett oesophagus**, intestinal type epithelium with goblet cells replaces normal squamous lining after years of acid exposure. That metaplastic segment progresses stepwise through dysplasia towards adenocarcinoma, so surveillance biopsies guide ablation or resection decisions. Goblet cells on biopsy therefore confirm Barrett change rather than simple reflux inflammation alone in patients.
steps.say: Reflux disease is a condition where acid repeatedly injures distal oesophageal squamous epithelium over many years of exposure. Barrett metaplasia develops because intestinal type epithelium with goblet cells replaces damaged squamous lining adaptively. Surveillance is important because dysplasia progresses stepwise towards adenocarcinoma in this metaplastic segment.

vis.alt: A diagram illustrating the pathological progression from normal oesophageal squamous epithelium through reflux oesophagitis, Barrett's metaplasia, dysplasia, to adenocarcinoma.
vis.caption: Barrett's oesophagus: stepwise progression from reflux to adenocarcinoma

steps.tx: Oesophageal cancers split by site, cause and histology into **squamous cell carcinoma** and adenocarcinoma for exam purposes. Squamous cancers arise in upper and middle thirds after tobacco, alcohol, achalasia or caustic injury exposure. **Adenocarcinoma** arises in the distal oesophagus from Barrett metaplasia with chronic reflux and obesity as major drivers. Both cancers present late with progressive dysphagia for solids then liquids, plus weight loss from reduced intake.
steps.say: Squamous cancers are tumours that arise in upper oesophagus after tobacco and alcohol injure squamous epithelium chronically. Adenocarcinoma is different because it develops distally inside Barrett metaplasia caused by reflux and obesity together. Progressive dysphagia develops because enlarging tumours narrow the lumen for solids before liquids.

steps.tx: **Peptic ulcer disease** develops when acid and pepsin overwhelm mucosal defence in the stomach or duodenum. Helicobacter pylori causes antral gastritis and duodenal ulcers, while NSAIDs block prostaglandins and cause gastric ulcers more often. Gastric ulcers require biopsy because cancer can masquerade as a benign ulcer on endoscopic appearance alone. **Duodenal ulcers** almost never become malignant, while complications include bleeding, perforation, penetration and gastric outlet obstruction.
steps.say: Peptic ulceration is a process where acid and pepsin overcome prostaglandin dependent mucosal defence in the stomach. Helicobacter infection is important because antral inflammation drives most duodenal ulcers in untreated patients worldwide. Gastric biopsy is required because malignant ulcers can look deceptively benign during endoscopy.

steps.tx: **Gastric carcinoma** divides into intestinal type and diffuse type, which behave differently in growth and spread patterns. Intestinal tumours form glands after Helicobacter related atrophy and metaplasia, usually arising in the distal stomach of older patients. Diffuse tumours contain **signet ring cells** that lose E cadherin and thicken the stomach into **linitis plastica** appearance. Virchow node, Krukenberg ovarian deposits and umbilical nodules indicate advanced metastatic spread in classic exam stems.
steps.say: Intestinal gastric cancer is a gland forming tumour that follows atrophy and metaplasia caused by Helicobacter infection chronically. Diffuse cancer is different because signet ring cells infiltrate widely and thicken the stomach wall diffusely. Metastatic signs help clinicians recognise advanced disease when Virchow nodes or ovarian deposits appear.
